$comment: SYNAPSE -- committed thresholds for the Interruption_Precision measurement (R8.5; design E6).
R8.5 requires the North-Star `interruptionPrecision` value to be COMPUTED from interruptions raised
during an executed run, and to DIFFER by at least `min_seed_divergence` between two seeds that raise
different interruption sets. That second clause is the falsifier a committed literal cannot satisfy:
a constant returns the same number for every seed, so its divergence is exactly 0 and the seed-
responsiveness audit reports `unresponsive`. This file holds the only number that audit compares
against, so the threshold is reviewable and diffable instead of being a literal in the checker
(the same rule as infrastructure/quality/replay-floors.yaml and ratchets.json).
Read contract. JSON rather than YAML so BOTH sides read it without a new dependency (I-1): Python
gates via json.loads(Path(...).read_text(encoding='utf-8')) (E-S13-07), and the TypeScript side via
frontend/src/lib/interruption-precision.ts::parseInterruptionPrecisionPolicy, which validates this
shape with Zod and refuses to substitute an in-code default. A missing or unparseable file is
reported `unavailable` -- non-passing, never a fabricated threshold (I-7).
`min_seed_divergence` is R8.5's own number, expressed as an absolute difference between two
precision values in [0, 1]. It is a floor on an OBSERVED difference, not a ratchet on a measurement,
so it carries no `measured_at`: nothing in this file claims that a measurement exists.
NOT MEASURED YET. No executed run has produced an Interruption_Precision value in this repository.
The wiring that will produce one (frontend/spec/effectiveness/harness.ts collecting interruptions,
and the effectiveness job in .github/workflows/frontend.yml running two seeds) is tasks 11.1/11.2.
Until it lands, computeInterruptionPrecision reports `indeterminate` and the scorecard carries no
number -- which is the honest state under I-7, not a pass.
